case_name: Manish Kanaujia And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy.

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Manish Kanaujia And 2 Others (husband, wife, and another)

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: The applicants sought to quash the criminal proceeding of Case No-844 of 2015 arising out of impugned summoning order dated 28.3.2015, and stay further proceedings in the court of ACJM-IV Lucknow.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking divorce to prove that the marriage has broken down irretrievably.
legal_principles.held: It is settled law that the parties have to come to an agreement realizing the irretrievable breakdown of their marriage and have mutually agreed and consented that their marriage be dissolved by a decree of divorce through mutual consent.
applicable_acts_sections: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

legal_principles.principle: A party seeking divorce must demonstrate that the marriage has broken down irretrievably.
legal_principles.held: The parties have now mutually agreed and decided that there is no reason for the continuance of the marital relationship & thus they have further mutually agreed upon by their own free will for dissolution of their marriage tie.

outcome.final_order: The application was allowed, and the entire criminal proceeding was quashed.
